paras: Gold miner, sailor, teacher, journalist – Prentice Mulford lived a dozen lives before he retired to a cabin in the New Jersey woods and wrote the essays that made him one of the first voices of New Thought. His message was bold and simple: thoughts are real forces, and the mind we cultivate shapes the life we live.

This beautifully designed annotated edition presents thirteen of his best essays and adds what today’s reader needs to put them into practice – with honest notes on what still holds up and what belongs to his time.

pd_statement: The essays of Prentice Mulford (1834–1891) first appeared from 1886 onwards in the series known as the White Cross Library. This selection, Thoughts Are Things, was published in London by G. Bell and Sons; this edition follows the printing of 1920. All of it is in the public domain. Spelling and wording are kept; obvious printing errors are corrected.
